title: The Good harvest that year
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：good　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 good 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the painter wrote of ① a good harvest that year in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② better than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it without complaint and gone home; it was the good ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the best harvest that year anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1981 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too good to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the good ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a good deed in the dark, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as good as the deed in the dark they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was good or not, and he said so.

By 1994 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something good, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite good; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the good ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1997, with great care, she wrote of another good harvest that year in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ better than anybody had expected. ⑩ The best deed in the dark in the whole studio, she said in 1999, was the one she could never quite name; the good ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 好（前置定语 a good harvest that year：1987 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件好的收成）
B. adj. 好／善良（比较级 better than：文中两处，一处比那年的好收成，一处比预想）
C. adj. 好／善良（最高级 the best：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 好（表语 too good to do：母亲觉得它太好，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 善良（前置定语 a good deed in the dark：叔叔把整件事称作一桩善良的善事）
F. adj. 善良（同级比较 as good as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩暗地里做下的善事相比）
G. adj. 善良（后置定语 something good：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 善良（受程度副词修饰 quite good：那位观者的评价）

items.q: the best harvest that year anybody
a good deed in the dark
The best deed in the dark in

answers.why: good 意为“好”，1987 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件好的收成”，此处作前置定语 a good harvest that year。
good 意为“好”，此处用比较级 better than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
good 意为“好”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最好的一件，故用最高级 the best harvest that year。
good 意为“好”，母亲认为这件东西“太好了，谁也用不上”，too good to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
good 意为“善良”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩善良的善事”，此处作前置定语 a good deed in the dark。
good 意为“善良”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩暗地里做下的善事一样善良”，同级比较用 as good as。
good 意为“善良”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“善良的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something good。
good 意为“善良”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当善良”，quite 修饰原级 good。
good 意为“善良”，1997 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要善良”，故用比较级 better than。
good 意为“善良”，母亲 1999 年说的是“整个画室里最善良的那一桩”，故用最高级 the best deed in the dark。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1987 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件好的收成。（a good harvest that year）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更好。（better than …）
母亲觉得它太好，谁也用不上。（too good to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩善良的善事。（a good deed in the dark）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩暗地里做下的善事一样善良。（as good as …）
到了 1994 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件善良的东西。（something good）
answers: In 1987 the painter wrote of a good harvest that year in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was better than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too good to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a good deed in the dark.
He said nobody would call it as good as the deed in the dark they had once had.
By 1994 the catalogue asked for nothing but something good.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 good 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1987 the painter wrote of a good harvest that year in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the best harvest that year in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too good to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a good deed in the dark, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite good, and everybody laughed.
The good ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
